notes: Layer-(a) gate-runnable assertions on the emitted verification PLAN (the gate has no MCP tools; live-fixture checks are layer b, run outside eval_gate).

cases.input: Produce the verification plan (checks only, no execution) for a Webflow homepage on staging site my-site.webflow.io, phase mode. The page has a hero video, a marquee, a contact form, and GSAP scroll scenes.

expects.assertion: The plan never claims Lighthouse (or any lab run) measures INP; INP is treated as field-only with TBT as the lab proxy (explaining this distinction is correct, not a violation).
The plan treats the PUBLISHED page (curl/headless Chrome) as the only evidence and never treats an API response as verification.

Performance (score, LCP, CLS, TBT, page weight) is measured with a throttled performance trace or the Lighthouse CLI and cites the saved file. lighthouse_audit, which has no performance category, is never named as the source of a performance number; naming it for accessibility, SEO or best practices is fine.
The loop is bounded at 3 fix rounds with an explicit escalation path carrying evidence.

cases.input: Produce the launch-mode verification plan for production publish of client-site.com (migrated from an old WordPress site).

expects.assertion: The plan frames the production checks as the exit condition of the Tier 3 publish, run against the custom domain post-publish.

cases.input: Plan the retirement of the custom script 'legacy-hotpatch.js' from a Webflow site (it exists as both a registered script applied site-wide and pasted in a page's freeform footer), and the verification that it is fully gone.

expects.assertion: The plan removes the script from BOTH the scripts registry and the freeform code block, and verifies removal by checking the PUBLISHED HTML for the script marker; removal from one surface alone is explicitly insufficient.

cases.input: Produce the visual-fidelity portion of the verification plan for a homepage whose design input is a Figma file, phase mode.

expects.assertion: The fidelity check compares the published-page screenshot against the DESIGN REFERENCE image (Figma get_screenshot), and the VLM judge scores against that reference: it never self-judges the page against the model's own taste.
The visual-fidelity check runs per breakpoint and names specific discrepancies (spacing, hierarchy, type scale, colour) that become fix-round tasks, rather than a single pass/fail with no detail.
The plan treats geometry+token equality as necessary but not sufficient, adding perceptual checks because token-equal pages can still read as un-designed.
